title: System V AMD64 ABI (calling convention)
summary: The System V AMD64 ABI is the standard calling convention for x86-64 on Linux, macOS, and most Unix systems. Integer/pointer arguments: RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9 (first 6), then stack. Floating-point arguments: XMM0-XMM7 (first 8), then stack. Return value: RAX (integer), XMM0 (float). Caller-saved: RAX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI, R8-R11. Callee-saved: RBX, RBP, R12-R15. Stack: 16-byte aligned before CALL. Red zone: 128 bytes below RSP (not clobbered by signal handlers).

structure.meaning: RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9 (in order). Additional args on stack (right-to-left).
Return value in RAX (and RDX for 128-bit).
Return value in XMM0 (and XMM1 for complex/long double).
RAX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI, R8-R11. Caller must save if needed across calls.
RBX, RBP, R12-R15. Callee must save/restore if used.
RSP must be 16-byte aligned before a CALL instruction.
128 bytes below RSP are not clobbered by signal handlers or interrupt handlers. Leaf functions can use this without adjusting RSP.
For variadic functions, AL = number of XMM registers used (0-8).

ext.example_decoded: Function prologue: PUSH rbp; MOV rbp, rsp
notes: System V AMD64 ABI is used by Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and most Unix systems.
Windows x64 uses a different ABI: RCX, RDX, R8, R9 for integer args; XMM0-XMM3 for float args.
The red zone is a unique feature of the System V ABI (not in Windows).
Functions must preserve RBX, RBP, R12-R15 (callee-saved).
